pamphlet_excerpts: Tone Shouldalways: Your tone shouldalways conveyenthusiasm forthe product orservice, yourcompany, and thecustomer.
Nothing Destroysbuyer: Nothing destroysbuyer confidencefaster than asalesperson who Customer Follow-Through Following up with customers is one of the most crucial skills.
Think Customers Loyal: Think of your customers as a loyal baseof friends who can help you increase sales, spread goodwillabout you and your company, and guide improvements.
Customers Welcome Chance: Customers welcome the chance to share their opinionsabout a product they purchased, and they appreciate that thesalesperson cared to ask.
step_by_step_procedure: Likely Feedback Negative: You are likely to get good feedback, even if it is negative, once customers have purchased theproduct and had a chance to try it out.
Effort Fulfill Unsatisfied: Make every effort to fulfill an unsatisfied customer’s needsin an efficient, quiet, and confident manner.
Chanceto Practice Super: This is your chanceto practice super salesmanship, to leap over tall obstacles andfind practical solutions to any and all problems.
Negativefeedback Requires: Any negativefeedback requires further follow-up once you have addressedthe customer’s concerns.

requirements.req_text: Explain why it is important for a salesperson to do the following: (a) Research the market to be sure the product or service meets the needs of customers. (b) Learn all about the product to be sold. (c) If possible, visit the location where the product is built and learn how it is constructed. If a service is being sold, learn about the benefits of the service to the customer. (d) Follow up with customers after their purchase to confirm their satisfaction and discuss their concerns about the product.

step_by_step_procedure: Sales Strategycareful: Give your sales strategycareful thought, because it will set the coursefor your business.

Identify Howyour Product: Identify howyour product stacks up to the competition, how it is similar to and different fromyour competition.
Think Canreach Portion: Think of how you canreach that portion of the market that yourcompetitors do not.

pamphlet_excerpts: Magazine Teen Entrepreneurs: Y&E: The Magazine for Teen Entrepreneurs* suggests thefollowing checklist to guide you through the steps of planningand delivering a winning.
STEP 1: Set a goal for your presentation. ■ Determine who your customer is (in this case, your counselor) and where you will meet. ■ Set a controlling purpose.
Want Customer Brainstorm: What do you want the customer to do? ■ Brainstorm a list of ideas and facts you want to communicate.
Out Doing Thesales: Find out how you are doing with thesales presentation by asking, “What else do you need toknow?” Keep asking for and answering questions until thecustomer.
step_by_step_procedure: Reassure Customer Right: Reassure the customer that you have the right solution bystating specifically how you can help.
Youknow Customer Wants: Even if youknow the customer wants to see a proposal first, is talkingto other salespeople, or is not ready to make a decision, askanyway.
Way Out Close: It is the only way to find out how close you are tomaking a sale.
Customer Responds: How the customer responds to this questionwill tell you exactly what you need to resolve before the person will buy from you.

Forrequirement Troop Raise: Forrequirement 5, you can help your troop raise funds, sellyour own services, or find work in retail sales.
Say Decided Troop: Let’s say you have decided to help your troop raise funds byselling lawn fertilizer in the spring and fall.
Dallas Texas Troop: One Dallas, Texas, Scout troop does this as its main fund-raiser each year.
step_by_step_procedure: Troop Starts Developing: The troop starts by developing a business plan that willensure brisk sales of fertilizer.
Research Retail Price: The Scouts research the retail price of fertilizer in local storesand compare that to the bulk wholesale price the Scouts willpay.
Products Soldin Bulk: Products soldin bulk toindustries, banks, railroads, airlines, governments, retail stores, and other largeinstitutions such as schoolsand hospitals.
Research Benefits Selling: The Scouts also research the benefits and selling points of thebrand of fertilizer they want to sell.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Interview a salesperson and learn the following: (1) What made the person choose sales as a profession? (2) What are the most important things to remember when talking to customers? (3) How is the product sold? (4) Include your own questions. (b) Interview a retail store owner and learn the following: (1) How often is the owner approached by a sales representative? (2) What good traits should a sales representative have? What habits should the sales representative avoid? (3) What does the owner consider when deciding whether to establish an account with a sales representative? (4) Include at least two of your own questions.

pamphlet_excerpts: Research Sales Career: As you research sales career opportunities, check the classifiedads in the newspaper.
Positions Salesbased: Notice how many positions are salesbased and how many different types of products people sell.
Free-enterprise Society: In a free-enterprise society like the United States, selling is thefundamental way business gets done.
Now Think Favorite: Now think about your favorite products, such as a favoritebrand of athletic shoes or type of jeans.
step_by_step_procedure: Pick Companyyou Particularly: Pick a companyyou particularly like or a brand name that you always buy.
Research Company Internet: Research that company on the internet (with your parent orguardian’s permission) or at your local library.
Out Whatyou Company: Find out whatyou can about the company, its philosophy, and its products.
Summer Salespositions: Summer salespositions providevaluable experience thatmany companiesseek when hiringfor career salespositions.
